subject: QBR prep: account clarity, run-rate assumptions, and ops handoffs
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: QBR prep: account clarity, run-rate assumptions, and ops handoffs

Team —

As part of the QBR next week I want a short, account-by-account readiness checklist we can hand to the ops and finance leads. I've uploaded a starter workbook (QBR_account_readiness.xlsx) to the Drive link below — please do not rework the format, just fill your rows. The goal: one row per named account with a 1-line current state, single numeric ask (delta vs. commit), next milestone, and risk tag (low/med/high).

Immediate asks (please):
- Owners (aditya, marissa, karthik): populate your accounts in the sheet by EOD Monday (2027-05-02). Include any changes to run-rate assumptions in run_rate_assumptions.csv.
- Markus: flag any accounts you want escalated for exec review and provide suggested mitigation.
- If you need documents for procurement or compliance, note them in the "needs" column — procurement@globalpay.com is looped for timelines.

Why this matters: we have three large pipeline moves that could materially change the QBR narrative if we don’t lock assumptions today (Acme, Linea Health, and BlueCloud). Short, factual lines only — we want to be able to paste these into slides.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=QBR-2027-account-summaries
HubSpot: hubspot://deal/HS-48392

Thanks —
Tessa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR prep: account clarity, run-rate assumptions, and ops handoffs

On 2027-05-01 09:12, Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Team —
>
> As part of the QBR next week I want a short, account-by-account readiness checklist ...

Will do. Quick notes on two accounts I'm owning:
1) Linea Health (Jacob Miller) — strong PoC signals, but procurement requires a signed DPA and SOC2 gap evidence. Jacob says procurement timeline looks like 3–4 weeks once we supply the artifacts; I've asked security to prioritize the requested evidence. Marking risk: MED.
2) BlueCloud — sales motion slowed due to a competing price commitment. I reduced the target this quarter by $120k in run_rate_assumptions.csv but put a contingent play in the notes column. Marking risk: HIGH.

I'll fill the sheet by EOD Monday and attach the run-rate CSV.

—Aditya
Head of Strategic Accounts

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR prep: account clarity, run-rate assumptions, and ops handoffs

Thanks — I've pushed a brief for each of my accounts into the workbook and added a one-paragraph summary to the "notes" cell for copy/paste into slides. A few operational things to call out:
- Acme (Sophie Tran): legal wants a negotiated SLA in order to sign. We have a redline in Acme_proposal_v2.pdf. I recommend we offer a 99.9% uptime SLA with an 8-hour response time for priority 1 incidents — legal is asking for 99.99%, which will materially change pricing.
- For accounts with procurement gating (Linea, Acme), I've added a link to the DocuSign/contract tracker column.

Action: Sophie is available for a 30-min readiness call Wednesday (2027-05-03) at 14:00 PT — I've tentatively held the slot.

-Marissa
Senior Account Director

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR prep: account clarity, run-rate assumptions, and ops handoffs

Tessa / team —

Added my accounts (logged edge-case notes for two: Nova Labs and Helio Retail). A couple of clarifications:
- Please use the risk tags consistently (LOW / MED / HIGH) and treat HIGH as "needs exec attention before QBR."
- For the run_rate_assumptions.csv I've included a conservative and stretch column — presenters should reference conservative in the QBR unless we have signed commitment.

I'll join the Acme readiness call and can take legal/technical questions.

Thanks,
Karthik
Regional Sales Manager

From: Jacob Miller <jacob@lineahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@globalpay.com
Date: 2027-05-03T16:25:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR prep: account clarity, run-rate assumptions, and ops handoffs

Tessa / Aditya —

Appreciate the clear asks. Procurement here — quick notes from our side:
- DPA + SOC2 evidence: we can accept the security questionnaire and the SOC2 summary. If Redwood can provide a short evidence bundle (control matrix + SOC2 summary) this week, procurement can accelerate the internal review and likely compress the timeline to ~10 business days.
- We have a budget committee meeting on 2027-05-17; if the evidence is in place by 2027-05-10 we'll be on track to get approval at that meeting.

I'll upload a purchase order template to your shared Drive and join the readiness call with Sophie if helpful.

Best,
Jacob Miller
Director of IT Procurement
Linea Health
